title: Missouri congressional-map ballot deadline — the US Supreme Court's window to stay the state ruling
source: NEWS: St. Louis Public Radio 2026-09-03 (fetched direct 2026-09-04) reports the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous ruling that the 2022 map governs the 2026-11-03 election and states 'the state faced a September 8 deadline to implement changes for the November 3 general election'; KSMU 2026-09-04 (fetched direct) reports the same court denied Secretary of State Denny Hoskins's stay request that morning and cites the UOCAVA 45-day ballot-mailing rule as the binding constraint. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by initial research from a PRIMARY source — the emergency application Hoskins v. von Glahn, No. 26A___ (S. Ct., filed 2026-09-04), published at ago.mo.gov and fetched direct, PDF text layer decompressed — which cites the date to a statute, 'ahead of a September 8 state-law deadline to alter the ballot, Mo. Rev. Stat. § 115.125.2', and in the same breath disclaims it as a constraint on the deciding court: 'Although this Court is not bound by it, Missouri has a state-law deadline of September 8 to alter the ballot'. STATUS STAYS ESTIMATE for the same mechanical reason as midterm-elections-2026-11-03 and boj-decision-2026-09-18: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has IR:/BLS:/FED:/TSY:/… and no slot for a statute or a court filing, so promotion would require a schema change out of this lane's scope. Understating the label only widens caution
notes: A seat-math resolution point, not a market event — filed low and expected to pass unnoticed by the tape. It is tracked because the midterm-elections-2026-11-03 ledger's leg 2 leans on a counterweight (ten states adopted new congressional maps for this cycle, estimated to net Republicans +6 to +10 seats) that this ruling directly reduces: Missouri's 2025 map, drawn to take the delegation from 6-2 to 7-1, will not be used on 11-03 unless the US Supreme Court stays the state ruling before ballots are set, and the map itself goes to a referendum on the 11-03 ballot. Silver Bulletin's FLIPR forecast page, updated 2026-09-04, names the ruling as improving Democratic chances. Discovered during the midterm-elections-2026-11-03 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). READ THIS DATE NARROWLY (initial research, 2026-09-05): 09-08 is a state ballot-administration deadline, NOT the date the question resolves. The applicant asks the US Supreme Court for 'a decision no later than September 14, 2026' and names the binding federal constraint as UOCAVA, 52 U.S.C. § 20302(a)(8) — overseas/military ballots mailed by September 19, tracked separately as missouri-uocava-ballot-mailing-2026-09-19. Justice Kavanaugh (Circuit Justice, Eighth Circuit) ordered respondent von Glahn to answer by noon 09-07; no action as of 09-05. The 'low' tier is measured, not assumed: VIX ran 15.20 → 14.32 → 14.53 across 09-02→09-04, spanning the ruling itself, with no index-level reaction.
